findings.title: Leaving the resting place redirects the body's call
findings.claim: The focus makes bodily disengagement from the resting place part of a chosen movement toward calling the Lord. The wider 10:12 contact sharpens the distinction: supplication can arise from crisis in many postures and then fade with relief, whereas the focus presents wakeful devotion as voluntary reorientation. A preceding 32:15 continuation is present only in legacy support.
findings.mechanism: The focus's non-attachment verb, bodily side, resting-place, and calling branches meet 10:12's side-posture call and its cessation after rescue. The contrast turns separation from mere sleeplessness into a relational choice; the cited 32:15 sequence is carried as an attributed local lead-in, not as the global trigger.
findings.reader_payoff: The bodily posture matters because it marks what the worshippers choose to leave and the address they choose to approach, not simply an hour or lack of sleep.
findings.containment: 10:12 supplies exact Arabic but no target morphology; its crisis/posture contrast is used at surface level. 32:15 appears only in legacy paraphrase, with no exact Arabic or morphology in this packet. The resting-place branch is an analogy to the side posture in 10:12, not a claim that 10:12 mentions a bed.

epistemic.reason: A trusted exact connection grounds the wider posture/calling contrast, while the 32:15 continuation and part of the spatial interpretation are legacy-attributed.

findings.title: Fear and hope hold invocation beside outward action
findings.claim: Fear and hope are paired around the focus's calling: apprehended harm pushes against complacency while hoped-for good draws the worshipper toward the Lord. Wider contacts place the same polarity beside life-giving water in 30:24 and fearful worship alongside provision-based spending in 22:35. Together with the focus's received provision followed by expenditure, this makes a devotional response that reaches beyond inward affect; it does not establish that affect causally produces giving.
findings.mechanism: The fear/calling/hope words in the focus meet 30:24's exact fear-and-hope pairing, while 22:35 joins worshipful remembrance, fear, and spending from provision. The focus itself orders provision before expenditure, so the parallel contexts illuminate a connected pattern of invocation and action.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired motives are not reducible to panic or appetite alone; they frame a response that includes both address and the handling of received resources.
findings.containment: The connection records supply exact target Arabic but no target morphology. Their parallel wording supports a wider pattern, not a causal claim that fear and hope make people spend. 22:35 is a related response, not a continuation of the focus's particular speakers.

epistemic.reason: The fear/hope pair and provision/spending contacts are supplied in exact connection targets; the synthesis joining affect to action remains an inference, and V12 supports are legacy-unbound.

findings.title: Received provision finds an outlet rather than ending at the recipient
findings.claim: The focus sets given provision before voluntary expenditure, allowing the recipient to be imagined as a passage rather than a terminal store. The exact wider 34:39 contact links spending with replacement by the Lord; a legacy-described exit blocked in 32:20 and corrective return before enclosure in 32:21 sharpen that image by contrast. The passage is an analogy, not the lexical meaning of the spending verb.
findings.mechanism: The focus's given-share branch meets its following expenditure branch; 34:39 supplies the concrete wider outflow-and-replacement pattern. The focus's registered outlet branch then meets the attributed 32:20/32:21 contrast, turning a local exit image into a bounded global resonance of voluntary circulation versus enclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: Giving reads as a route by which provision continues onward, not simply stock disappearing from its first recipient.
findings.containment: The prior cross-run support marks this proposal reject, which remains visible. The wider global trigger is 34:39, not 32:20: 32:20 is inside the 32:11-20 pericope and cannot establish global scope alone. 32:21 is present only as a legacy paraphrase. The actual focus form means spending; the tunnel/exit branch is analogical, and replacement does not prove a direct return to the giver.

epistemic.reason: 34:39 provides exact wider Arabic for spending and replacement, while the 32:20/32:21 contrast is legacy-attributed and the prior support grade is reject.

findings.title: The object determines whether turning away is responsive
findings.claim: The focus's withdrawal from the resting place is not good merely because it is detachment. In 32:22, the wrongdoer turns from remembered signs; in 32:30, the messenger is told to turn from persistent rejecters. The changing objects support an inference that fidelity lies in choosing what to leave and what to remain attached to.
findings.mechanism: The focus's non-attachment and bodily-side words meet exact same-surah constructions of turning away after a reminder and turning away from rejecters. The recurrence changes the moral value of withdrawal with its object; the focus movement is not a universal endorsement of separation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish wakeful devotion from refusal of guidance without treating every act of turning away as virtuous.
findings.containment: The HFT roles and unresolved context roots at 32:22/30 remain attributed; no gloss or facet is invented for them. 32:22 has an exact connection target but no target morphology. Deliberate moral contrast is an inference; ordinary idiom without a designed contrast remains live.

epistemic.reason: Exact context Arabic, HFT word coordinates, and focus returns support the comparison, while the context branch identities and moral design remain attributed/inferred.

The focus spending branch also meets the legacy-described 32:17 hidden recompense, while a registered nurturing branch under Rabb meets the crop-growth context.
findings.reader_payoff: A resource leaving its first holder may still belong to a sustaining process whose effects reach another recipient.
findings.containment: The authored connection calls 32:27 only a broad context for God's giving; agricultural provision and human spending may remain separate examples. 32:17 is paraphrased only in legacy support, not supplied with exact Arabic here. The rain and outlet branches are material analogies, and the Rabb-as-nurturing activation is contextual, not a direct lexical meaning or identification of the human giver.

epistemic.reason: HFT supplies exact focus/32:27 coordinates, but the water-to-spending relation is analogical, the connection itself limits the context to broad giving, and 32:17 is legacy paraphrase only.

findings.title: Wakeful separation as a contained clearing-flow analogy
findings.claim: In an exploratory material analogy, bodily separation from the resting place can resemble residue cast aside by a current; provision and spending then supply a flow-and-outlet frame, with 32:27 directing water toward a dry receiving place. This is a secondary image, not a translation of the focus verb.
findings.mechanism: The registered foam/residue branch of the focus root meets the focus's provision and outlet branches and the traced water movement to barren land. The contact allows a clearing-and-flow image to be perceived across bodily, economic, and agricultural domains.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader may see wakefulness and generosity as forms of clearing and onward movement, while retaining the ordinary meaning of leaving beds and spending provision.
findings.containment: The source labels this reading exploratory and explicitly branch-distant. The 32:27 connection row calls the water/crop contact only a broad context for God's giving, and the human/agrarian domains may be separate. The foam branch must never be presented as the direct lexical meaning of تتجافى; the other focus branches and barren-land trigger are contextual analogies.

epistemic.reason: Although the trace has exact focus and 32:27 coordinates, it joins a distant foam branch to hydraulic and economic imagery, and the connection record itself limits 32:27 to broad context.

friction_notes: The exact connection targets 10:12, 22:35, 30:24, 34:39, 32:22, and 32:27 supply Arabic but not target morphology; connections are used as surface-level contacts only.

32:15, 32:20, and 32:21 occur only in legacy support paraphrases in this packet. 32:20 is inside the declared 32:11-20 pericope and cannot establish a global finding by itself; 34:39 is the concrete wider trigger for the outlet reading.

The 32:17 hidden-recompense point is also legacy paraphrase only. It is retained with that attribution; 32:27 supplies the exact wider material contact but is qualified by a connection note calling it broad context for God's giving.

HFT context branches for 32:2, 32:5, 32:22, 32:27 remain unresolved registry nominations. Their exact supplied coordinates, roles, and focus returns are retained as attributed, with no invented glosses or facets.
RZQ/B003 rain, NFQ/B003 passage, JFW/B003 foam, and Rabb/B002 nurturing are contextual or material analogies, not direct meanings of the focus forms; hydraulic clearance remains exploratory.

The prior cross-run support for the outlet proposal carries grade reject. It remains visible as counterevidence; the qualified retention depends on the distinct 34:39 contact, not that prior grade or 32:20 alone.
